summary: The SOP is well structured, and most of its sources check out live, but the cutover and rollback paths have gaps that could cost data or leave the team without a timed way back: IaC is never sequenced against the gcloud upgrade, rollback time and mechanics sit outside the window budget, and the 'no writes before go/no-go 2' assumption isn't enforced. Several gates also can't be checked from evidence as written (queryid baselines across major versions, pg_stats counts, MD5 roles, and the Block 3 gates), and a few Cloud SQL requirements are missing (the pg_squeeze floor, the path where replicas aren't included, and the automatic pre-upgrade backup).

findings.claim: Changing database_version in Terraform is itself an upgrade path, but the SOP never says when the IaC PR is applied relative to the gcloud upgrade. It also never says how to reconcile Terraform state afterward or how to check the plan for a destroy-and-recreate. Applying early would start an unrehearsed production MVU, and a bad plan could delete the instance.
findings.evidence: SOP B1-11: "IaC for the target version... Agent opens the PR, a person applies"; G1.7: "IaC changes exist as reviewed PRs, planned but not applied". The Block 3 runbook only uses "the rehearsed command" (gcloud). S-01 (fetched): "To upgrade the major version of the database using Terraform, you must set the database_version argument" and "If +/- appears next to your google_sql_database_instance resource after changing database_version, don't proceed with terraform apply. This will delete your instance and all of its data."
findings.suggested_fix: Add a runbook step that says exactly when the IaC version change merges. It should merge after the gcloud upgrade, as a no-op reconcile, and the plan must show only an in-place (~) change or no change. Also require deletion_protection=true, and forbid applying the IaC PR before the window.

findings.claim: Rollback before reopening is the main safety net, but its duration isn't in the window budget, and its mechanics are reduced to 'point the apps back'. Cloud SQL rollback means building a new instance with matching flags, restoring, re-adding replicas one by one, and repointing every consumer to a new connection name. G2.6 times only the restore, and the timing happens after the window clock stops.
findings.evidence: SOP: "restore the pre-upgrade backup to a recovery instance on the source version [S-01], then point the apps back." Step 13: "Stop the window clock." Step 14: "Restore the pre-upgrade backup to a new instance and time it." G2.1 covers only "in-window steps within 75% of the window". S-01 (fetched): "Create a new Cloud SQL instance using the major version... Set the same flags and instance settings that the original instance uses... Add your read replicas... update your application with details about the recovery instance and its read replicas."
findings.suggested_fix: Rehearse and time the full rollback: create the instance with matching flags and settings, restore, add replicas, repoint the pooler, apps and CDC, and run validation. Require upgrade time plus rollback time to fit the window, or have the business approver sign for the overrun in the decision record.

findings.claim: The rollback says no writes happen before go/no-go 2. But smoke tests run and CDC consumers start on new slots before that point, and both can write or advance downstream offsets. A rollback could then lose smoke-test writes or leave consumers with offsets that don't exist on the restored instance.
findings.evidence: Runbook: "Create new slots and start consumers | CDC owners" then "Bring up the pooler and routing, then run validation and smoke tests | App on-call | Go or no-go 2: the point of no return". Rollback: "Before go or no-go 2: ... No writes have happened, so nothing is lost."
findings.suggested_fix: Require smoke tests before go/no-go 2 to be read-only, or list their writes so they can be replayed. Add rollback steps for CDC consumers: reset offsets, recreate slots on the recovery instance, or re-snapshot.

findings.claim: G2.4 and G3.3 compare top statements to a baseline keyed by queryid. Postgres says queryid isn't stable across major versions, so 14 and 18 statements can't be matched reliably. The plan diff also needs query text, which the guardrail bans from baselines, so the gate could be marked done without a real comparison.
findings.evidence: SOP step 3: "a statement baseline by queryid with no query text"; G2.4: "The top 50 statements run within 2x of baseline"; guardrail: "Statement baselines use queryid without query text." https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/pgstatstatements.html (fetched): "it is not safe to assume that queryid will be stable across major versions of PostgreSQL."
findings.suggested_fix: Define a cross-version key that a person controls, such as a named list of representative statements with parameters kept outside agent sessions. Say who runs EXPLAIN on both versions and what redacted evidence goes into the tracker.

findings.claim: The Cloud SQL extension floors for 18 list only PostGIS 3.6.0 and pg_ivm. They leave out the pg_squeeze 1.8 requirement from the same cited page, so a team using pg_squeeze would miss a required pre-upgrade step.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Cloud SQL 18 needs PostGIS 3.6.0 [S-01]. `pg_ivm` blocks the MVU [S-01]." S-01 (fetched): "Before you perform an in-place major version upgrade to PostgreSQL 16, 17, or 18, upgrade the pg_squeeze extension for all of your databases to version 1.6, 1.7, or 1.8 respectively."
findings.suggested_fix: Add pg_squeeze 1.8 to the extension floors, and add its quote to S-01 in sources.json. Recheck the S-01 page for any other per-extension floors.

findings.claim: The SOP only covers replicas upgraded together with the primary. When replicas are left out, Cloud SQL requires upgrading them first, that can't be rolled back, and the replicas serve no data until the primary is upgraded. None of this appears in the rehearsal, the runbook or the rollback, and external replicas can't be upgraded in place at all.
findings.evidence: SOP step 2: "Add replicas to the clone if the plan upgrades them with the primary." The Block 3 runbook has no replica step. S-01 (fetched): "If you use read replicas and choose not to include replicas with your major version upgrade, then you must upgrade the read replicas before you upgrade the primary instance. After you upgrade a replica, you can't roll back the database version of the replica. The replicated databases of an upgraded replica are available only after you upgrade the primary instance." and "External replicas can't be upgraded in-place."
findings.suggested_fix: Make replica handling (include, upgrade first, or drop and recreate) a decision-record item. Add the matching runbook, rehearsal and rollback steps for each option, including the read-routing impact while replicas are unavailable.

findings.claim: G1.4 requires every MD5 role to be moved or waived, but the SOP itself says the MD5 role list can't be read on Cloud SQL. Its substitute, testing logins on the clone, can't find MD5 roles because PG 18 still accepts MD5 logins and only warns when an MD5 password is set. The gate can only pass on someone's say-so. The pg_authid claim is also Cloud SQL-specific but stated for all managed services.
findings.evidence: SOP: "On managed services nobody can read `pg_authid` [S-05], so test every password login on the rehearsal clone." G1.4: "Password-login roles use SCRAM, or each MD5 role has its owner's waiver". S-05 is a Cloud SQL page: "customers cannot create or have access to users with superuser attributes". S-17 (fetched): "CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE now emit deprecation warnings when setting MD5 passwords."
findings.suggested_fix: Name the evidence for G1.4, for example a provider answer, a rotation log that resets every login role's password under scram-sha-256, or the provider's IAM-auth inventory. Scope the pg_authid claim to Cloud SQL.

findings.claim: The G2.3 stats count and the missing-stats query use pg_stats, which shows only tables the caller can read, in the current database. A database owner without SELECT on other roles' tables gets an undercount, sees readable tables listed as missing, and has no per-database instruction. G2.3 could pass or fail on incomplete evidence.
findings.evidence: SOP: "a stats count run as the database owner: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stats WHERE schemaname NOT IN (...)". G2.3: "every table has planner stats". https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/view-pg-stats.html (fetched): "This view allows access only to rows of pg_statistic that correspond to tables the user has permission to read".
findings.suggested_fix: Run the count in every database. Compare it against the number of tables the role can read, and list the tables it can't read separately. Alternatively, compare pg_class.reltuples and last_analyze for coverage instead of relying on pg_stats alone.

findings.claim: The Block 3 gates have no Evidence column, unlike every other block. 'Validation passed' and 'Close-out is done' can be marked on someone's say-so.
findings.evidence: SOP Block 3: "| Gate | Done when |" with "G3.1 | Production runs the target version, writes are open, and validation passed" and "G3.4 | Close-out is done". Section 1: "each one names the evidence it needs."
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Evidence column to the Block 3 gates, for example validate.sql output, consumer owner confirmations with lag readings, a 24-hour plan diff, and a close-out checklist with links.

findings.claim: Unverified items are flagged, but no gate requires them to be settled before cutover. G0.7 only requires the questions to be sent, and several Appendix B questions (replica hostnames and stats, PITR across the upgrade, transfer mode) aren't tied to any rehearsal step or gate.
findings.evidence: G0.7: "Questions for the provider have been sent, and someone owns tracking the replies". Appendix B: "These are Unverified until the provider answers or the rehearsal shows the answer." No Block 2 or Block 3 gate references Appendix B.
findings.suggested_fix: Map each Unverified item to the gate or rehearsal step that settles it. Add a Block 2 exit gate requiring each one to be answered, shown by the rehearsal, or waived by a named approver.

findings.claim: B0-01 has agents search code for connection strings and link evidence. Connection strings in repos often contain passwords, so this puts production credentials into agent sessions and tracker links, against the guardrail. There's no redaction rule.
findings.evidence: B0-01: "Code search across every org for DB connections: connection strings, hostnames, env var names, role names..." with artifact "Repo rows with evidence links". Guardrail: "No production or clone credentials in any agent session."
findings.suggested_fix: Tell agents to record only file paths and line references for matches, never the values. Add a rule that any embedded secret found is reported to its owner for rotation, not copied into the tracker.

findings.claim: G1.3 assumes every CDC connector has a version that supports the target, but the SOP gives no path when none does. One connector the SOP itself mentions, Flink CDC, documents support only up to PostgreSQL 14 in a source this template already holds.
findings.evidence: G1.3: "Every CDC connector has a version that supports the target, staged and approved by its owner". Step 10 cites Flink CDC startup modes [S-27]. S-26 (fetched): "| [postgres-cdc](postgres-cdc.md) | <li> [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org): 9.6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14".
findings.suggested_fix: Cite S-26 in Block 0 and Block 1. Define what happens when no supported version exists: a tested-unsupported waiver from the owner, a connector replacement, or a decision-record change.

findings.claim: The SOP notes the 14.24 output_plugin_libraries change but only says to record it. It never freezes provider maintenance, for example with a Cloud SQL deny period. A maintenance update between rehearsal and cutover could change the source minor and break CDC that uses a non-default plugin, and the flags page has no entry that lets customers add plugins.
findings.evidence: SOP: "If the source minor is behind the provider's current one, record it." S-21 (fetched): "By default, only the output plugins shipped as part of PostgreSQL (pgoutput and test_decoding) are included in output_plugin_libraries. Installations that rely on other output plugins must add them after updating the server". S-11: "The page has no output_plugin_libraries entry."
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Block 1 task to set a maintenance window or deny period through cutover, and to apply any pending minor update before the rehearsal. Require the rehearsal to run on the same minor version that production will have.

findings.claim: S-10 has status 'changed' in sources.json, which sources.md says means claims citing it should be treated as Unverified. The SOP cites it as fact and says all sources were rechecked. I rechecked the page and the wording still holds, split by an HTML entity, so the label and the quote list are what need fixing. S-10 is also about maintenance updates, not the MVU.
findings.evidence: sources.json S-10: "status": "changed". sources.md: "A source whose quotes have moved is marked `changed`... Treat claims that cite it as Unverified". The live page reads "maintenance updates automatically install the latest extension binaries on your instance's underlying software, they don't automatically update the extension's database catalog" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/extensions).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the S-10 quote so the checker can match it, and rerun the checker. For the post-MVU ALTER EXTENSION step, cite general pg_upgrade behavior or label it Inferred.

findings.claim: The SOP cites S-18 for removing db_user_namespace and trace_recovery_messages, but S-18's quote list has neither. The facts are correct on the live page, but the Verified claim isn't backed by its sources.json row.
findings.evidence: SOP: "`old_snapshot_threshold`, `db_user_namespace` and `trace_recovery_messages` in PG 17 [S-18]". S-18 quotes: "old_snapshot_threshold", "adminpack" only. The live PG 17 notes say "Remove server variable trace_recovery_messages since it is no longer needed" and "The feature, db_user_namespace, was rarely used."
findings.suggested_fix: Add both quotes to S-18 in sources.json, and check other multi-fact citations, such as S-22 for datallowconn and composite types, the same way.

findings.claim: The rollback depends on the pre-upgrade backup, but the SOP never says Cloud SQL creates it automatically, how to identify it, or that clone deletion and cleanup must not remove it. 'Confirm backups' at T-7 is undefined, and 'retention ends' doesn't match upgrade backups, which persist until someone deletes them.
findings.evidence: SOP: "T-7 days | Freeze migrations, confirm backups"; close-out: "record when the pre-upgrade backup's retention ends." S-01 (fetched): "Cloud SQL automatically makes two on-demand backups, called upgrade backups... the pre-upgrade backup, which is made immediately before starting the upgrade" and "upgrade backups persist until you delete them".
findings.suggested_fix: State that the MVU takes the pre-upgrade backup, how to find it by label, what 'confirm backups' checks, and who decides when to delete the upgrade backups.

findings.claim: The cutover steps say to stop writers and drain CDC to zero lag, but give no way to block new connections or end stragglers and no lag threshold. The lag query also includes physical slots, which have no confirmed_flush_lsn, and background WAL can keep logical lag from ever reaching exactly zero.
findings.evidence: Runbook T-0: "Turn on maintenance mode and stop writers. The census query shows only expected sessions." T+5: "Drain CDC to zero lag and record the LSN". The step 5 query selects all of pg_replication_slots with no slot_type filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the mechanism for blocking connections (pooler pause, CONNECTION LIMIT, or revoking CONNECT) and the command for ending remaining sessions. Filter the query to slot_type = 'logical', and define drained as each consumer confirming the recorded LSN.

findings.claim: The XID-age guidance waits until ages 'approach 2 billion' before freezing. That's too close to the wraparound limit, where Postgres starts warning and then refuses writes, to leave time for a freeze before an upgrade window.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Ages approaching 2 billion need a freeze before anything else (Inferred, general Postgres knowledge)."
findings.suggested_fix: Set a concrete, earlier action threshold, for example well above autovacuum_freeze_max_age, such as 1 billion. Cite the PostgreSQL routine-vacuuming documentation instead of labeling it Inferred.

findings.claim: The SOP, the reading guide and the kit disagree on which sections are invalid on a replica. The SOP omits 8b. The kit says section 4 and 5b show nothing on a replica, even though publications (4b) and unlogged-table catalog rows (5b) do replicate.
findings.evidence: SOP: "sections 4a, 4c and 6b describe the replica". Reading guide line 10: "Sections 4a, 4c, 6b and 8b describe the replica... Catalog sections (... 4b, 5 ...) replicate and are still valid." precheck.sql line 18: "section 4 and 6b are per-server and show nothing on a replica"; line 114: "Unlogged tables (... empty on read replicas)".
findings.suggested_fix: Settle on one list, such as the guide's, and update the SOP step 3 text and the kit comments to match.

findings.claim: The adapting section undercounts the Cloud SQL-specific content. Step 6 (slot deletion), step 9's superuser expectations, and the T+10 cancel rule are also provider-specific, and several S-05 facts are stated for all managed services. Its claim that sections 0 to 8 are plain Postgres contradicts section 1 being the provider precheck.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Swap in the provider's own command. Keep sections 0 to 8, which are plain Postgres." and "Replace Block 2 steps 1, 2, 7 and 14, and the Block 3 rollback". Step 9: "managed services don't give customers superuser [S-05]". S-05 is the Cloud SQL users page.
findings.suggested_fix: List every Cloud SQL-specific step and claim, including steps 6 and 9, the T+10 checkpoint and G0.3. Scope the S-05 claims to Cloud SQL, and say 'sections 0 and 2 to 8'.

findings.claim: Communication is reduced to 'comms have gone out' and a comms plan that the SOP doesn't define. There's no on-the-night messaging for start, go/no-go outcomes, rollback or reopening, and no escalation contacts.
findings.evidence: B1-10: "Runbook, rollback plan and comms plan"; Block 3 entry: "The change ticket is approved and comms have gone out." The runbook outline has no comms rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Add comms rows to the runbook (start, each go/no-go, rollback decision, reopen) with an owner and audience, and list the minimum contents of the comms plan.

findings.claim: The SOP depends on files that weren't part of this review: the tracker schema, which defines the gate rows and evidence, and the plugin rules and hook that it says enforce the guardrails. I couldn't verify that the enforcement exists.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Gate rows live in the tracker ([tracker-schema.md](tracker-schema.md))" and "These are enforced by [the plugin's rules and hook](../plugins/pg-major-upgrade/)." Only assets/precheck.sql and one skill reference file exist under review/plugins/pg-major-upgrade.
findings.suggested_fix: Include tracker-schema.md and the rules and hook in the review set, or soften 'enforced by' until a reviewer has checked them.

findings.claim: A single local test result is labeled Inferred and has no evidence link. A reader can't tell whether 'pg_upgrade --check passes, real upgrade fails' was observed on Cloud SQL or on community pg_upgrade.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Our test kit saw one such function pass `pg_upgrade --check` and then fail the real upgrade (Inferred from one local test)."
findings.suggested_fix: Link the test's reproduction and state the versions and environment, or label it as an internal observation with its scope.

findings.claim: G1.1 covers blockers from both the provider precheck (G0.3) and the kit (G0.4), but its only evidence is a kit rerun, so provider precheck errors could be marked fixed without a provider rerun. G1.5's evidence, merged exporter PRs, doesn't show that dashboards work on the target.
findings.evidence: G1.1: "Every blocker from G0.3 and G0.4 is fixed... | Rerun of kit sections 6a to 6g". G1.5: "Monitoring queries and dashboards work on the target version | Exporter PRs merged".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a provider precheck rerun with no ERROR entries to G1.1's evidence. For G1.5, require a screenshot or query output from the dashboards against a target-version instance, such as the CI database or the clone.
